Chapter 198: The Scarf Hand-Knit by Lin Xiuhong

It was late and quiet at night.

Lin Xiuhong suddenly knocked on the door and entered Li Luo's bedroom.

Li Luo had been typing away on Yan Zhusheng's laptop when he saw his mom walk in with a solemn expression.

"What's wrong, Mom?" Li Luo stopped what he was doing and looked at Lin Xiuhong, puzzled.

"Turn around." Lin Xiuhong sat on the edge of the bed and patted Li Luo, signaling him to face her. "I want to have a heart-to-heart with you."

"Oh." Seeing her extremely serious and earnest expression, Li Luo didn't make any jokes and obediently turned to face his mom to listen attentively.

Seeing his attitude, a satisfied look appeared on Lin Xiuhong's face, and she began to speak, "You're earning a lot of money now, more than your parents, and our whole family is happy for you."

"But, we also need to understand that no money just falls from the sky. This is also something you've earned through your own hard work."

"Do you remember one of your cousins? That Wei Dongrong from before, his family also has another cousin. That cousin's family got their start relying on some short-term windfalls."

"It was fine at first, making millions a year, living the good life. But their family didn't manage their own child well, pampering him with extravagant meals every day."

"Later, the child was spoiled. He spent money extravagantly and had no normal concept of money. He wouldn't wear any clothes that weren't over ten thousand yuan, and his sneakers had to be limited editions."

"And after that? Later on, their family business couldn't continue because the general environment changed, and their income was suddenly cut off."

"If they had managed to save the millions they made each year, they would still have lived a comfortable life."

"But their son's spending habits were already deeply ingrained and couldn't be changed. In just a few short years, the entire family's fortune was squandered."

"Li Luo, what I'm saying, can you understand what I mean?"

"Mhm." After listening, Li Luo nodded seriously. "Don't worry, Mom, I don't spend money recklessly. I'm saving all of it."

At this point, an idea struck Li Luo, and he decided to test his mom's attitude ahead of time. So, he continued, "I was just thinking, didn't we buy a condo in Bihai Lanting? If the subway is built there in the future, will the property value increase?"

"So if I earn enough money later on, could I buy another condo near the subway entrance?"

"Or maybe buy one of those storefronts, like your breakfast shop. Wouldn't that also be very profitable in the future?"

"Whether it's writing my book or writing songs, I rely on talent and inspiration to make a living, and that stuff is bound to run out one day."

"But something like a storefront can bring in a stable income for real. Don't you think so, Mom?"

Prompted by Li Luo's words, Lin Xiuhong was taken aback.

They were having a good talk, how did it suddenly turn to investing in real estate and storefronts?

But on second thought, she felt that what her son said seemed to make a lot of sense.

Leaving the money sitting there was just leaving it sitting there.

And according to what Li Luo said, this month's royalties would be even higher.

So if there was a stable investment direction, it would be a good safeguard for the future.

However, Lin Xiuhong still said, "Your task right now is to focus on your studies first. As for writing books and songs, your mother doesn't understand it, so you'll have to figure it out yourself. I won't give you any misguided advice."

"As for how to use the money you've earned, whether to buy property, we'll have to see. Your dad and I need to discuss it further."

"Also, this is just something for us family members to talk about. Don't go blabbing about it to others. You know the saying about not flaunting your wealth, right?"

"Don't worry, Mom, I won't talk about it." Li Luo nodded and said, "I was just bringing it up. You can talk to Dad about it. You two can decide what to do specifically."

"Alright, let's leave it at that for now." Seeing her son being so sensible, Lin Xiuhong showed a gratified expression, stood up, and patted his shoulder. "I won't disturb you anymore. Remember to go to sleep early."

On Sunday at noon, after taking Ying Chanxi to the breakfast shop for a free lunch, the two of them slung on their schoolbags and returned to Bihai Lanting.

Once they got to Apartment 1502, Li Luo planned to continue writing in the afternoon, while Ying Chanxi had to go to school for her competition class.

Yesterday, in order to go shopping with Li Luo in the afternoon, she had even asked her teacher for a leave of absence and missed Saturday afternoon's competition class. This afternoon, she had to make up for yesterday's coursework.

But just before Ying Chanxi left, Li Luo called out to her and asked, "What's your favorite color?"

"Hmm?" Ying Chanxi looked at him strangely. "Why are you asking?"

"Just pick one." Li Luo added, "White, yellow, or red, pick one."

"Oh... then red." Ying Chanxi glanced at the scarf around Li Luo's neck that she had knit herself and couldn't help but say it.

"Okay, then wait here for a moment." Li Luo said as he went back into his bedroom. A moment later, he came out with a light red scarf in his hand and draped it around Ying Chanxi's neck. "Wear it. It's for you."

Ying Chanxi stood there stunned, looking down at the scarf on her, feeling a little touched for a moment. "What made you think of giving me this?"

"Ahem... my mom gave it to me." Li Luo said honestly. "How does it feel?"

"It's very comfortable." Ying Chanxi touched the scarf, her lips pressing together before curling up slightly. If she had a tail, it would probably be wagging high in the air by now. "But, how did you know I would choose red?"

"It means we're on the same wavelength."

"Hmph." Ying Chanxi rolled her eyes at him, then put on her schoolbag and shoes, walked out the door with a light spring in her step, and waved goodbye. "I'm off then."

After seeing Ying Chanxi off, Li Luo returned to his bedroom and looked at his dashboard, where the average subscription count had risen to 13,000. He couldn't help but feel a bit dazed.

It had to be said that before he started writing this book, although he had fantasized about such results, he came back to reality after the initial subscription numbers came out.

His skill level was only enough to write an ordinary, cliché webnovel. Being able to reach the "boutique" tier was purely due to his mature application of experience and tropes from his past life. But Li Luo never imagined that his serendipitous song, "Annual Rings," would have such a massive impact.

It directly changed the future course of his book.

You see, in this era, there were only about twenty or thirty books on Qidian's main site with over ten thousand subscriptions that were still being serialized.

A glance showed that they were basically all by top-tier authors.

Li Luo was now like a husky that had infiltrated a wolf pack. Relying on the surge at the beginning of the month, he had occupied the top spot on the new book chart for a long time.

Unfortunately, his results themselves couldn't quite beat those Great Gods and Platinum authors. After holding the top spot on the bestseller chart for three days at the beginning of the month, the numbers slowly dropped, finally settling at seventh place on the overall chart.

For this book to reach ten thousand subscriptions was indeed outside of Li Luo's plans.

His original intention was just to earn a little pocket money for himself to make his high school life a bit more comfortable.

He had originally planned to try making big money during his university years.

He just never expected that by a twist of fate, relying on the song "Annual Rings," his connection with Yan Zhusheng, and Yuan Wanqing building the bridge, he would complete such a magnificent feast of traffic.

One could only say that sometimes, fate is just that magical. When luck arrives, you can't stop it.

The only thing that made Li Luo a little regretful was that his book was in the entertainment genre. Although it was set in a fictional world, it still plagiarized many entertainment works that existed in reality.

In addition, it was an urban novel with a multi-female lead background, so it would probably be a bit difficult to sell the publishing rights.

He would likely only be earning subscription money.

However, Li Luo knew how to be content. With the start-up capital provided by this book and selling songs, if he could buy one or two storefronts before the subway entrance was completed...

Then his future comfortable little life would be completely secured.

Thinking of this, a relieved smile appeared on Li Luo's face.

Just as he had been writing for about two or three hours, he heard the sound of the front door opening.

Xu Youyu was back.

"Li Luo! What's for dinner?" Xu Youyu knocked on the bedroom door, then opened it and peeked her head in, asking expectantly, "What ingredients should I buy? I'll go to the market."

"Just buy whatever you feel like eating." Li Luo closed the writing software and stood up. "What do you want to eat today?"

"I want chicken wings, and also beef brisket."

"Then you should go buy it soon. Beef brisket takes a long time to cook."

"How about asking Zhusheng what she wants to eat? Let's invite her over for dinner this afternoon," Xu Youyu said. "But in that case, you'll have to come with me to buy groceries, or I won't be able to carry everything by myself."

"Oh, got it. I'll give her a call on the way." As Li Luo said this, he suddenly asked again, "Senior, which do you prefer, white or orange?"

"White, I guess. Why?" Xu Youyu was walking towards her bedroom, planning to put down her schoolbag, and then asked, "Suddenly making me choose a color... let me guess, are you thinking of buying me clothes?"

"You're quite clever, but unfortunately, you guessed wrong." Li Luo wagged a finger, then took out a white scarf. "Here, for you."

"Wow," Xu Youyu's eyebrows shot up, a little surprised. "Do you know what it means to give a girl a scarf?"

"It means you're good friends."

"Heh, then thank you for now, my good friend." Xu Youyu covered her mouth and chuckled lightly, but she didn't reach out to take it. Instead, she leaned her head forward slightly. "Help me put it on. My hands are full."

Xu Youyu was carrying her schoolbag with both hands at that moment, and it did look rather inconvenient.

So Li Luo helped her put on the scarf.

The white scarf, paired with the new warm-yellow down jacket she was wearing, looked quite nice.

Especially with this circle of white scarf resting above her chest, it accentuated her beautiful silhouette, making it hard to look away.

"It feels like a good fit." Xu Youyu looked down, then smiled. "How thoughtful of you to even think of giving me this."

"Well, you gave me pants yesterday, so it's only right for me to return the favor."

"But where did you buy this?" Xu Youyu curiously touched the scarf. "It feels really comfortable to wear, the quality is great."

"My mom knit it by hand."

"Eh?" Xu Youyu was stunned and suddenly became a bit embarrassed. "Is-is that so? Auntie is truly skilled... Um... that... I'm going to the bathroom first."

After putting her schoolbag back in her bedroom, Xu Youyu slipped into the bathroom.

Closing the door, Xu Youyu looked at herself in the mirror and couldn't help but pat her slightly reddened cheeks.

"Honestly... giving away a scarf his own mother hand-knit without making it clear when he gave it." Xu Youyu looked at the white scarf around her neck and couldn't help but shake her head with a wry smile.

Then she touched the warm texture of the scarf again, her lips pursing slightly. "What a strange feeling."

Hmm... I can write this into my book in the future.

This is a rare research experience, too.

(End of Chapter)
